text:
maya: quick design sync 0— I want to align on validation hierarchy + quick-fix UX for the routing editor. There's been a lot of debate: inline badges, top-of-panel summary, toasts, and simulator-level warnings. also motion concerns for list reorders (reflow vs transform).

samir: big picture: validation should be contextual first. Inline warnings next to the offending rule, with an optional summary banner listing unresolved issues. toasts can remain for ephemeral success/errors but not for conflicts you need to act on.

olivia: +1 for inline-first. UX question: inline badge affordance 1 should be actionable. idea: small chevron on badge opens a micro-panel with two quick-fixes: "Bump priority" and "Add guard" that mutate the rule inline. keeps flow tight.

jess: accessibility: micro-panel must be keyboard operable and announce changes (aria-live). suggested announcement copy: "Priority conflict on 'Block PII'. Quick actions: bump priority, add guard." After applying action announce result: "Priority increased; rule moved to position 3." Also support reduced-motion preference when animating reorder.

marcus: dev concerns: inline quick-fix should avoid heavy network round trips. implement optimistic UI and a lightweight validation pass client-side for common fixes. also prefer transform-based animation for reorder (GPU accel) instead of layout reflow to avoid jank.

maya: good call on optimistic. UX microcopy debate: should quick-fix copy be imperative or explanatory? e.g., "Increase priority" vs "Increase priority to resolve tie". shorter is better but must be clear. want to test two variants in mock.

olivia: i'll prepare two microcopy variants in the mock: terse (imperative) and contextual (short explainer). we'll A/B in internal testing.

jess: reduced-motion: when user has prefers-reduced-motion we should skip animated shuffles and use an immediate reorder with an aria notification: "Rule X moved to position Y". when motion allowed, use a short transform animation (150-200ms) with easing. record preference in user settings.

samir: simulator integration: preview should flag conflicts pre-run with inline badges and include a deterministic-resolve button that runs a local heuristic to propose fixes. we should not wait until after the full sample runs.

preview-bot: preview-sim: heuristic-resolver added to staging. run `preview-sim --policy 900 --heuristic-propose` to surface suggestions. logs: /staging/sim/900/heuristic.

marcus: performance note 3: micro-panels should be rendered via portal to avoid layout thrash when opening many at once. also lazy-load guard editor components to keep initial JS small.

maya: copy guidelines: keep action label one verb phrase; add a 1-sentence explanatory tooltip on hover. examples to test: "Increase priority" + "Resolves ties by moving this rule earlier" vs "Make routing deterministic" + tooltip.

jess: aria sample strings I'll draft: 1) when badge appears: "Warning: priority conflict on 'Name'"; 2) when quick-fix panel opens: "Quick fixes for 'Name'"; 3) after action: "'Name' moved to position N". will drop into the spec.

samir: acceptance criteria: 1) inline badge appears for conflicts and includes quick-fix trigger; 2) quick-fix panel supports keyboard, optimistic update, and undo; 3) simulator pre-run offers heuristic proposals; 4) reorder animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and use transform-based animation otherwise.

olivia: I'll mock micro-panel states + both microcopy variants. also include motion-off state screenshot. target mock drop Thursday EOD.

maya: also let's add a subtle audit trail entry when quick-fix is applied (who did it and what change) for Dedicated/Private customers. we can show this in the rule details flyout.

marcus: backend will emit an event for quick-fix actions so audit logs can pick it up. we'll include a small correlation id in the optimistic response so UI can reconcile.

jess: small accessibility nit: the badge color shouldn't be the only cue. include an icon and an assistive text node for screen readers. ensure contrast >= 3:1 for badge background and text.

maya: thanks all. olivia, jess, marcus, samir 0 please sync on the spec after mocks. i'll coordinate a quick internal usability test with 6 engineers to compare microcopy variants + motion preferences next week.

olivia: on it.

maya: thanks team :raised_hands:
